definition: The angle at a point on a circle made by lines to the two ends of a diameter; it is always $90^{\circ}$.
The angle between a tangent and the radius drawn to its point of contact; it is always $90^{\circ}$.
The angle made at the centre of a circle by two radii; it is twice any angle at the circumference that stands on the same arc.
Angles at the circumference that stand on the same chord, on the same side of it; they are always equal.
A quadrilateral with all four corners on one circle; its opposite angles add up to $180^{\circ}$.
The angle between a tangent and a chord, at the point of contact, equals the angle that chord makes at the circumference in the segment on the other side of the chord.
